name: Congenital Aortic Valve Atresia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Congenital Aortic Valve Atresia Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Complete absence or imperforate aortic valve orifice confirmed by echocardiography or cardiac catheterization
Hypoplasia or underdevelopment of the left ventricle detected by imaging
Dependence on patent ductus arteriosus for systemic circulation evidenced clinically or by imaging
Absent or markedly diminished aortic valve auscultatory sounds

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of absent aortic valve orifice with left ventricular hypoplasia and systemic circulation dependent on patent ductus arteriosus
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiographic and clinical findings in the neonatal period.

laboratory: Arterial blood gas showing metabolic acidosis
Elevated lactate levels indicating tissue hypoxia
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating absent aortic valve orifice and left ventricular hypoplasia
Cardiac MRI or CT confirming valve atresia and ventricular morphology
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and pulmonary vascular markings
genetic: No specific gene identified; may be associated with congenital heart defect syndromes
other: Dependence on prostaglandin E1 infusion to maintain ductus arteriosus patency

distinguishingFeatures: More extensive left heart hypoplasia including mitral valve and ascending aorta
Presence of aortic valve leaflets with severe stenosis rather than complete atresia
Left ventricular hypertrophy rather than hypoplasia

redFlags: Severe cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of cardiogenic shock in neonate
Rapid progression to heart failure within first days of life
